protocol: Parallel-Run Protocol v2; one selected method lane; at most 3 experiments
method_lane: H-APART-6 OTSP: fold-visible fault-strike orientation transport into independently measured, multi-scale topographic and gravity lineaments; no SGMC input and no peer-raster input
ranking_note: Expected improvements below are pre-experiment design priors, not measured scores, projections, or organizer-confirmed results.

ranked_candidates.title: Orientation-Transported Scale Persistence (OTSP)
specific_layers: Official competition numerical feature Band 12 det_elev and Band 13 iso_grav_anom
USGS 3DEP-derived dem10_hgm50_max and dem10_onesided3 cached rasters
Fold-visible existing_faults.tif only (re-derived separately inside holdout)
ranked_candidates.physical_signature: Axial strike agreement between a local tangent estimated only from visible fault pixels and topographic/gravity contact tangents that persist from 200 m to 1200 m Gaussian scale; structure-tensor coherence and independent lineament strength suppress isotropic texture.
ranked_candidates.why_off_catalogue: A buried or distributed parallel splay can preserve the strike of a nearby mapped master fault while its own trace appears only as a weak, scale-persistent topographic or potential-field edge. The candidate is emitted off the visible trace with a pixel-exact catalogue mask and a collar-tempered distance term.
ranked_candidates.difference_from_repo: H-APART-2 has endpoint cones, relay density and independent 8-azimuth worm maxima, but it does not transport the measured tangent of each visible fault to require axial agreement with blind topographic and gravity contacts at several scales.
ranked_candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Parallel road/rail embankments and aligned alluvial-fan channels.
ranked_candidates.mimic_control: Existing TIGER road deconfounder remains in the base surface; OTSP additionally requires multi-scale persistence and gravity-contact agreement, which surface infrastructure and drainage should not consistently produce.
ranked_candidates.implementation_cost: Medium; cached official layers, deterministic CPU structure tensors, no new download
ranked_candidates.data_obtainability: READY: all inputs are already hash-pinned and cached by scripts/prepare_data.py

ranked_candidates.title: Signed Piedmont Curvature-Reversal Persistence
specific_layers: USGS 3DEP dem10_curv_absmax, dem10_resid_range, dem10_onesided and 1 m LiDAR crest/toe channels
ranked_candidates.physical_signature: Paired curvature sign reversal and antislope step that persists across 100 m, 300 m and 700 m profiles at low-slope basin-depth hinges.
ranked_candidates.why_off_catalogue: Young low-slip piedmont splays can be omitted where scarps are subtle or discontinuous under alluvium; persistence and basin-depth gating target those traces rather than obvious mapped range-front scarps.
ranked_candidates.difference_from_repo: H-APART-2 uses one-sided relief and crest-toe amplitudes but does not require signed curvature reversal at three profile scales.
ranked_candidates.data_obtainability: READY: USGS 3DEP derivatives are cached and hash-pinned

ranked_candidates.title: Radiometric Contact / Potential-Field Edge Phase Concordance
specific_layers: USGS GeoDAWN K, Th, K/Th and U/K channels
Official RTP magnetic and isostatic-gravity anomaly layers
ranked_candidates.physical_signature: Co-located directional edges in radiometric ratios and magnetic/gravity phase, with a demagnetization sign consistent with hydrothermal alteration.
ranked_candidates.why_off_catalogue: A concealed structure can juxtapose altered and unaltered rock or focus alteration without a mapped surface break, while remaining visible as concordant geochemical and potential-field boundaries.
ranked_candidates.difference_from_repo: H-APART-2 includes potassic amplitude and demagnetization gates, but not directional phase-concordance of the radiometric contact itself with both magnetic and gravity edges.
ranked_candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts unrelated to faulting and airborne-survey seams.
ranked_candidates.data_obtainability: READY: GeoDAWN products are cached from a pinned public mirror with official USGS provenance

ranked_candidates.title: Thermal-Residual / Clay-Cap Boundary Cross-Validation
specific_layers: DOE GDR #1391 2 m temperature probes and spring/geothermometer table
ranked_candidates.physical_signature: Locally robust thermal residuals coincident with electrical-conductivity boundaries and a sharp structural lineament, rather than broad thermal halos.
ranked_candidates.why_off_catalogue: Upflow may identify permeability on buried faults that have no mapped trace; requiring a conductivity boundary and lineament avoids treating every warm measurement as a fault.
ranked_candidates.difference_from_repo: H-APART-2 smooths probe/spring impulses and applies a structure gate, but does not estimate leave-neighborhood-out thermal residuals or require directional clay-cap boundary concordance.
ranked_candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Shallow groundwater circulation, irrigation and measurement-cluster sampling bias.
ranked_candidates.data_obtainability: READY: sanitized GDR #1391 tables are cached and hash-pinned
